usageNotes: Use this to open a VNC console session to a running QEMU VM — the response returns a one-time ticket, port, and TLS cert that a VNC client (or the Proxmox noVNC web client) uses to connect. The caller must hold the VM.Console privilege on the VM. The VM must be in a running state on the specified node; calling this against a stopped or migrating VM will fail.

examples.summary: Open a VNC proxy session for VM 101 on node pve1

tips: The returned ticket is short-lived — use it immediately to establish the VNC connection before it expires.
Set websocket: true when your client will upgrade to WebSocket transport; this is required for the serial-terminal path but harmless for standard VGA console access.
The generate-password param is deprecated and ignored; do not pass it in new code.
Use the returned cert fingerprint to validate the TLS connection and avoid MITM on the VNC channel.
If you need the SPICE protocol instead of VNC, use the sibling spiceproxy endpoint.
